A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a model for diffractive hard scattering, which is based on the assumption of independence between hard and soft interaction, and which is valid at small x.

we have developed a model-independent approach for studying rapidity gap survival effects and their dependence on proton-proton impact parameter in exclusive double-gap diffractive pp collisions at the LHC.
we have developed the theoretical framework to study the production of heavy states (H=dijets, heavy quarks and Higgs bosons) in double-gap diffraction at the TeV scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RGS probability is strongly suppressed at TeV energies, even if the hard interaction is assumed to be completely free of soft interactions.

the survival of the diffractively produced rapidity gap in the pp scattering process depends on the impact parameter of the collision, and that the probability for a diffractive process is suppressed by a factor of the order of 1/2 at large impact parameters.

the RGS probability is strongly suppressed at TeV energies, and the diffractive production of high-mas systems is likely to be dominated by double-Pomeron processes, which are not described by our model.
